messages:
Alyssa: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike of 503s from /v1/generate over the last 5m. Alert `api-5xx` fired and routed to product-oncall, but this looks infra-y. Where should I look for traces and a quick PromQL/log query to narrow origin? cc @Kevin :thinking:

Tom: If it's 503s, first suspects are ingress proxy or upstream saturation. Routing note: api-5xx currently maps to product-oncall by default. Quick dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/requests-5xx (filter by path=/v1/generate). Traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/search?q=service:ingress+path:/v1/generate

Jenn: Quick PromQL to split client vs upstream: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",path="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (service,upstream)`
Also check logs in LogUI: filter `status:503 AND path:"/v1/generate"` and sample request_id.

Kevin: We can change PD mapping if needed. PD mapping lives in infra/team-routing repo: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/team-routing/blob/main/pd_mappings.yml. Current snippet:```yaml
service: api-5xx
routes:
  - team: product-oncall
  - fallback: infra-oncall
```
We can add an `escalation: infra-oncall` or make infra primary for sustained bursts.

Alyssa: Could we also add a short suppression for transient bursts? Thinking `burst_threshold` so we don't wake people for a 30s blip. :thinking:

Tom: Yep — suggestion: require >50 errors in 60s or sustained rate for 5m before routing to infra. Something like `burst_threshold: 50, window: 60s, sustained_window: 5m`. Jenn — want to open the PR? :thumbsup:

Jenn: On it. I'll open a PR against infra/team-routing and tag @Kevin for review. For immediate triage, we can assign infra-oncall for 10m. Use `/pd escalate api-5xx --to infra-oncall` or run `/pd trigger` if you want an incident record.

ops-bot: Incident bot: Alert `api-5xx` triggered at 1862001234, routed to product-oncall. Escalation candidate: infra-oncall.

Kevin: I'll add infra-oncall as a secondary recipient for a 10m window while we investigate, then revert. Done — added temporary secondary.

Alyssa: Thanks — attaching one suspicious trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/abcdef123456 — shows upstream latency spike coinciding with 503s. I'll update if it repeats.

Tom: If it repeats, open an incident in #incidents and tag @eng-sre. Good catch.
